About Agile Defense
 
At Agile Defense we know that action defines the outcome and new challenges require new solutions. That’s why we always look to the future and embrace change with an unmovable spirit and the courage to build for what comes next.
 
Our vision is to bring adaptive innovation to support our nation's most important missions through the seamless integration of advanced technologies, elite minds, and unparalleled agility—leveraging a foundation of speed, flexibility, and ingenuity to strengthen and protect our nation’s vital interests.

Summary
 
 Target Effect Pairing (TEP) gives USPACOM Joint Fires AI recommendations, through the Maven Smart System, that commanders can trace, explain, and audit. Those recommendations are only useful if operators can compare options and see the reasoning in time to act on it. That puts weight on both ends of the stack: services that recompute quickly when inputs change, and interfaces that present dense comparisons and geography clearly.

 You build across both. On the back end that means microservices, message-driven architecture, and workflow and agent orchestration. On the front end it means React and TypeScript interfaces, including geospatial views. You implement the Senior UX Designer's workflow designs and work with the program's architects, the Systems Integration Engineer, and the Product Manager/Fires SMEs.

 The team works in two locations, requirements are still taking shape, and all work happens in secure facilities.

 What Success Looks Like 

 Objective 1: In the first 90 days, ship a feature end to end in the program's environment 


 Your code is reviewed, merged, and deployed in the secure environment.

 You can explain the operational workflow behind the feature to a Fires SME in their terms.

 You know where the program's architecture and interfaces constrain your work, and you build within them.


 Objective 2: Build services that recompute fast enough for operators to explore options 


 When an operator changes an input, the updated recommendation arrives inside their workflow rather than after it.

 Performance is measured, and regressions are caught before release.

 Each orchestration step leaves a record that can be traced during an audit.


 Objective 3: Build interfaces that let operators compare recommendations and see the reasoning 


 Comparative and geospatial views match the design, and usability testing confirms operators can read them.

 From the interface, an operator can trace any recommendation to the inputs and logic behind it.

 Changes requested after operator feedback ship in the next increment.


 Objective 4: Raise engineering quality across both locations 


 Your tests and reviews catch defects before government testing does.

 Documentation lets an engineer in the other location pick up your work without a handoff meeting.

 The code you write is covered by automated tests that run in the delivery pipeline.


 What You Bring 

 Minimum Qualifications 


 Proven ability to drive progress and create clarity in fast moving, ambiguous environments. Ability to maintain required TS/SCI access.


 Preferred Skills 


 You have built and shipped full-stack applications in production, with back-end services in Go, Java, or Python.

 You have built microservices or message-driven systems that held up under real load.

 You have built data-dense interfaces in React and TypeScript that people relied on to compare options.

 You have built geospatial visualizations with CesiumJS, Mapbox, or similar.

 You have worked with workflow or agent orchestration frameworks.

 You have tuned performance and can point to the measured result.

 You have built from a designer's work and pushed back constructively when something wouldn't work.

 Experience in secure or classified DoW environments, or with Maven Smart System, is a plus.


 WORKING CONDITIONS 

 All work takes place in secure facilities. Two positions are based in the National Capital Region and travel 50% of the time. One is based in Honolulu with the USPACOM-based development team.

 
 Environmental Conditions 

 Work is primarily performed in professional office, Government, and technical development environments. This position requires regular on-site collaboration in the San Diego area, including work with Government and development stakeholders at or in support of NIWC-Pacific. Periodic travel may be required to support operational stakeholders and other mission activities. Work may occur in secure facilities with restrictions on personal electronic devices and remote connectivity.

 Strength Demands 

 Sedentary to light physical demands associated with professional office and technical work environments. Occasional movement or transport of laptops, documents, and other standard work materials may be required.

 Physical Requirements 

 Regular use of computers and standard office equipment; ability to participate in meetings, technical working sessions, and collaborative development activities for extended periods; ability to communicate effectively in person and through approved electronic means; and ability to travel as required.

  



Our Core Values
 
Employees of Agile Defense are our number one priority, and the importance we place on our culture here is fundamental. Our culture is alive and evolving, but it always stays true to its roots. Here, you are valued as a family member, and we believe that we can accomplish great things together. Agile Defense has been highly successful in the past few years due to our employees and the culture we create together. 
 
What makes us Agile? We call it the 6Hs, the values that define our culture and guide everything we do. Together, these values infuse vibrancy, integrity, and a tireless work ethic into advancing the most important national security and critical civilian missions. It's how we show up every day. It's who we are.
 
Happy - Be Infectious. Happiness multiplies and creates a positive and connected environment where motivation and satisfaction have an outsized effect on everything we do.
Helpful - Be Supportive. Being helpful is the foundation of teamwork, resulting in a supportive atmosphere where collaboration flourishes, and collective success is celebrated.
Honest - Be Trustworthy.Honesty serves as our compass, ensuring transparent communication and ethical conduct, essential to who we are and the complex domains we support.
Humble - Be Grounded.Success is not achieved alone, humility ensures a culture of mutual respect, encouraging open communication, and a willingness to learn from one another and take on any task.
Hungry - Be Eager.Our hunger for excellence drives an insatiable appetite for innovation and continuous improvement, propelling us forward in the face of new and unprecedented challenges.
Hustle - Be Driven.Hustle is reflected in our relentless work ethic, where we are each committed to going above and beyond to advance the mission and achieve success.
 
Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities
